name: rtk-dangerous-actions-blocker
description: Deprecated: use block-destructive-commands, which shares this policy's destructive-command table. rtk#1007. Same table as block-destructive-commands: blocks root/home/.git deletes, force/delete/mirror pushes, reset --hard, clean -f, switch --discard, IaC destroy, cloud deletes, DB drops, lockouts; asks rm -rf off rtk's safe list, one named kubectl delete, bare lease, stash drop, prunes; dry-run flags pass. Own rows block credential-file reads (.env, keys, ~/.ssh) and echo or inline *_API_KEY/_SECRET/_TOKEN. Skips file rows in container exec. [Session-enforced in Cursor by a beforeShellExecution hook: a matched command is denied before it runs (witnessed blocking on Cursor, 2026-08-24). The hook needs git, a Python 3.11+ (python3, python or py; the Windows Store stub is skipped) and a usable bash resolved from PATH. The hook entry sets `failClosed`, which Cursor's hooks documentation (cursor.com/docs/agent/hooks) says blocks the action when the hook fails to run, so a hook that cannot start refuses the command. If the guard itself crashes, the hook returns `permission: "ask"`, which beforeShellExecution honours. Repo-wide enforcement at commit time and in CI still needs `chock sync`.]
